effects.name: beat
effects.summary: A cover, logo, card or play button that pulses with the music of a page player: it scales, shakes and glows, or sends out rings, on the beat.
effects.looks: While the <audio> or <video> plays, the element swells by zoom on every beat of the kick drum and settles back over duration, with a soft halo in color around its rounded shape, or a ring that travels outward from its edge for each beat. by bass follows the bass line instead of single beats, by level the loudness of any sound, such as a voice. The element itself stays live DOM: links and buttons work, text stays sharp. Paused, nothing moves and nothing draws.

effects.name: gradient
effects.summary: A living background of four soft color blobs or of aurora curtains, mixed in OKLab, without banding, with a light film grain.
effects.looks: Four soft blobs of color drift slowly over the element on looping paths that take minutes to repeat, their edges bent by noise. They lean toward the pointer and shift as the page scrolls. Colors mix in OKLab, so two colors meet through a clean middle instead of a muddy gray, and every pixel is dithered, so smooth ramps show no bands. A light film grain sits on top; set grain to 0 for a clean gradient or around 0.08 for a film look. The aurora style draws the first color as a night sky and the other three as curtains of light that wave along it, sharp at their lower edge and rising in uneven rays.

effects.summary: A dot grid behind a hero or in a card that answers the pointer: dots near it grow, move aside or glow, then settle back.
effects.looks: An even grid of small dots, plus marks or squares, the same pattern a CSS radial-gradient background draws. effects.name: ambient
effects.summary: A soft glow in the colors of the frame around a video or an image, like ambient mode.
effects.looks: Around the box lies a large, heavily blurred copy of the frame’s main colors that fades out past the edge. While the video plays the light follows its frames a few times a second and flows from color to color; on pause it stands still. The video itself stays DOM: native controls, captions, fullscreen and picture-in-picture work as without the effect. As a shadow the light falls below the box instead, narrower than it, like a drop shadow in the picture’s colors under a cover or a card. Best on dark pages; the glow is not cut by an ancestor’s overflow, unlike box-shadow.
effects.target: video, img

reducedMotion.note: The light changes only on start, pause and seeking, flowing for a second, so it does not breathe with the video.

presence.note: The glow fades with the page as it leaves.

effects.touch: The same as with a mouse; the quality tiers lower the update rate on weak devices.

notes.low: At most 4 updates a second from an 8-cell grid.

cost.gpu: One plane the size of the box and its glow, one read of a tiny texture per pixel.
cost.memory: A few kilobytes. Each update draws the frame into a 16 × 9 canvas and reads it back on the CPU.

effects.name: hover-preview
effects.summary: Over a list of projects, the picture of the item under the pointer follows the pointer, stands beside the item or holds a fixed place.
effects.looks: While the pointer is over an item, its picture floats at the pointer: it appears from a slight shrink, trails behind with a stretch along the motion, a soft bow and a tilt from the speed, and crossfades into the next item’s picture with a small settle. Leaving the list fades it out. In beside mode the picture stands next to the hovered item’s text and glides from row to row; in fixed mode it holds one place by the list and only crossfades. The list stays as you wrote it: text, links, focus and selection are the DOM, nothing is hidden.

effects.name: sequence
effects.summary: An image sequence scrubbed by scroll, frame by frame, from a poster .
effects.looks: The image becomes a flip book driven by the sticky section it sits in: scrolling down plays the frames forward, scrolling up plays them back, the way product pages take a device apart. Each frame is framed by the object-fit and object-position of the . With blend, neighboring frames mix by the fraction of the index, so a short sequence of 24 to 36 frames moves smoothly.
effects.target: img, the poster frame

params.description: What drives the frame: pin of the sticky section, viewport progress, or frame alone.

params.description: Progress at which the first frame shows.

params.name: end
params.description: Progress at which the last frame shows.

params.name: frame

params.name: blend
params.description: Mix neighboring frames by the fraction of the index.

params.name: ease
params.description: Smoothing of the index behind scroll; 0 follows scroll at once (Lenis already smooths it).

params.name: cache
params.description: Decoded frames kept around the current one, two of them ahead in the scroll direction.

params.name: density
params.description: Share of the frames loaded: 0.5 loads every second one and the others show the nearest.

params.name: resolution
params.description: Longest side in px a frame is decoded at; larger frames shrink while decoding.

frames.note: Scroll draws its own frames; a frame that finishes decoding asks for one, and ease keeps drawing until the index settles. None at rest.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the shows its poster and not a single frame is downloaded. The poster is what people with reduced motion and without WebGL see, so choose it on purpose; another still frame for them is a with .

presence.note: Fades with the page transition; a keyed flight carries the frame shown at the time.

effects.touch: Works as on desktop: scroll drives it.

notes.medium: Up to 4 decoded frames, decoded at up to 1440 px.
notes.low: Every second frame, up to 2 decoded frames at up to 960 px.

cost.gpu: Two texture reads per pixel of the box; one upload of the frame per drawn frame at most.
cost.memory: The compressed bytes of every frame it loads, cache decoded frames on the CPU and one texture of a frame on the GPU (two with blend). An atlas holds its pages instead, .webp, .avif or .ktx2 images, and compressed .ktx2 pages take 4 to 8 times less GPU memory. Under Save-Data or on 2G it loads a quarter of the frames at up to 960 px.

effects.name: expand
effects.summary: The image of a card grows to fill its sticky stage as the section scrolls.
effects.looks: Between start and end of the pin a copy of the image grows from the box of its card to the box of the sticky stage, usually the whole screen, easing in and out. Its corners go to radius, object-fit frames it anew at every size, so cover never stretches, and the content swells a little on the way and lands at its size. It then holds the screen; when the section lets the stage go, it leaves with it. With out below 1 it folds back into the card before the pin ends. Scrolling up plays it all backward.

effects.name: lightbox
effects.summary: A click opens an image full screen: its copy flies out of the grid, pages and zooms.
effects.looks: A click lifts the image out of the grid towards the viewer and carries it to the center of the screen while its crop opens to the full picture, the rest of the grid sinks back and the backdrop darkens; the large file crossfades in after the flight. Inside, arrows, buttons and swipes page, and a double click, the wheel or a pinch zoom. Escape, the close button, a click on the backdrop, a swipe down or scrolling the page brings it back to its place the same way.

effects.name: flipbook
effects.summary: The page images of a container become a book whose pages bend as they turn.
effects.looks: Pages show as a spread of two, or one on a narrow box. Closed on its cover the book stands in the middle of the box; as the cover turns the book slides so the open spread is centered on its spine, and closed on the back cover it stands in the middle again. A turning page bends around a fold from the spine, the fold is shaded and a shadow falls on the page below. A page follows the finger or the mouse from a corner or an edge and, let go, finishes the turn or falls back; a click on a closed book opens it and a click on a half of a spread turns forward or back, and with tabindex on the container the arrows, PageUp, PageDown, Home and End turn too. effects.name: spin
effects.summary: A product turns by drag through a series of photos taken around it.
effects.looks: A horizontal drag picks the frame from a series shot in a circle, and with rows a vertical drag picks the viewing angle. The frame follows the pointer and stops where it is let go; with inertia a flick coasts on and eases out onto a whole frame, neighbor frames cross-fading on the way so it slows without stepping. effects.name: glitch
effects.summary: A digital glitch in short bursts: blocks slide sideways, color channels split, scanlines flicker.
effects.looks: For a fraction of a second the picture breaks up: horizontal blocks jump sideways and wrap around, red and blue part ways, scanlines darken and the frame flickers, with flashes of static. effects.name: scrub
effects.summary: A video scrubbed by scroll: its time follows the sticky section it plays in, forward and back.
effects.looks: While the section pins its stage, scrolling down plays the video forward and scrolling up plays it back, the way product pages turn a device or take it apart. Every frame the browser decodes crossfades from the one before for as long as the frames take to come, at most blend, so the picture moves smoothly even when seeks lag behind the scroll and stays sharp when they keep up. Frames are framed by the object-fit and object-position of the video. Encoding decides how smooth it is: give the file a keyframe every few frames (ffmpeg -g 5, or -g 1 for every frame) and enough frames for the scroll, 24 to 30 a second, since a few frames stretched over a long scroll step however they blend; keep it short and at most 1080p, with no sound; a file from a phone or an editor has a keyframe every few seconds, and every seek backwards then decodes up to that many frames.
effects.target: video, muted, with preload="auto" and a poster of its first frame

params.name: by
params.description: What drives the time: pin of the sticky section, viewport progress, or position alone.

params.name: start
params.description: Progress at which the scrubbed span begins.

params.name: end
params.description: Progress at which the scrubbed span ends.

params.name: position
params.description: Place in the span shown when by is manual, for a tween or a slider.

params.name: from
params.description: Time in the video the span starts at.

params.name: to
params.description: Time in the video the span ends at, in seconds; auto is the end of the video.

params.name: ease
params.description: Smoothing of the time behind scroll; 0 follows scroll at once (Lenis already smooths it).

params.name: blend
params.description: Longest crossfade from one decoded frame to the next; frames that come quicker fade quicker. 0 cuts.

params.name: resolution
params.description: Longest side in px a frame is copied at; larger videos shrink on the GPU.

frames.note: Scroll draws its own frames; a decoded frame asks for one, and ease and blend keep drawing until the time and the crossfade settle. None at rest, and no seeks while the video is off screen.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the video shows its poster and is never seeked. People with reduced motion and without WebGL see the poster, so choose it on purpose.

presence.note: Fades with the page transition.

effects.touch: Works as on desktop: scroll drives it.

notes.medium: Frames copied at up to 1440 px.
notes.low: Frames copied at up to 960 px.

cost.gpu: Two texture reads per pixel of the box, one frame copy and upload per decoded frame.
cost.memory: The video as the browser buffers it, and two copied frames on the GPU. A 4 second 1080p clip with a keyframe every 5 frames is about 2 to 4 MB as H.264 or VP9.

effects.name: chroma
effects.summary: A video shot on a green or blue screen, played over the page with the screen keyed out.
effects.looks: The product or presenter stands on your page as if the video had transparency, from one ordinary MP4 or WebM that plays in every browser, Safari included, where WebM alpha does not play and HEVC with alpha is hard to make. Pixels close to the screen color turn clear, with a soft ramp at the edge; green that the screen threw onto the subject is taken out, fully at the edge and by spill inside, and the edge itself is averaged over a few neighboring pixels so it does not crawl. Before the video plays its poster shows keyed the same way.
effects.target: video on a green or blue screen, muted for autoplay, with a poster of its first frame; your own play button and captions next to it

params.name: by
params.description: color keys out the screen param; auto reads the screen color every frame from whichever top corner of the frame is greener, for unevenly lit footage.

params.name: screen
params.description: Color of the screen to remove, green by default; #0047bb for blue.

params.name: similarity
params.description: How far from the screen color a pixel may be and still turn clear.

params.name: softness
params.description: Width of the soft ramp from clear to opaque past similarity; 0 cuts hard.

params.name: spill
params.description: Share of the screen’s hue taken out of the subject, all of it at the see-through edge; 0 keeps every color as shot.

params.name: blur
params.description: Distance in px of the neighbors each pixel’s key is averaged with; 0 is off.

params.name: crop
params.description: Share of the frame cut off at the top, right, bottom and left, for light stands and the screen’s end.

frames.note: One frame per video frame while it plays and is on screen, at the video’s own rate; none while it is paused, before it plays or off screen.

reducedMotion.note: Keyed as usual: keying is not motion. Whether the video plays is up to the site; under reduced motion, start it paused and let the visitor play it.

presence.note: Fades with the page transition.

effects.touch: The same as on desktop; tapping works as the site’s own buttons do.

notes.low: No blur: one texture read per pixel instead of five.

cost.gpu: Five texture reads per pixel of the video’s box with blur, one without, and a small color transform.
cost.memory: One video frame on the GPU, and the poster until the video plays. The video itself is as large as the file: no second copy with alpha.

effects.name: liquid
effects.summary: The pointer leaves a fluid trail on a photo that settles back like water.
effects.looks: Where the pointer passes, the picture bends as if seen through moving water: a wake follows the path, spreads, drifts a little and fades out over duration, after which the copy matches the image again. Unlike ripple, which draws rings around a hovering pointer for as long as it stays, liquid reacts only to movement, follows the path the pointer took and goes still on its own.
effects.target: img, video

params.name: style
params.description: water refracts the picture by the slope of the wake and lights its edges; smear drags the picture along the path like a finger through wet paint; prism drags it and splits the trail into red and blue fringes.

params.name: strength
params.description: How far the trail moves the picture: 0 turns the effect off.

params.name: radius
params.description: Width of the trail around the path.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time the trail takes to settle after the pointer stops.

params.name: swirl
params.description: How much the wake drifts along itself as it fades: 0 keeps it in place.

params.name: shine
params.description: Light on the edges of the wake in water style: 0 refracts without light.

params.name: split
params.description: Width of the color fringes in prism style: 0 leaves the colors together.

params.name: resolution
params.description: Cells of the trail along each side of the image: more is finer and costs more CPU.

frames.note: Only while a trail is settling, about duration after the last move; none at rest, and a still pointer draws nothing.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the image stays DOM and nothing loads for it.

presence.note: Fades with the page transition, which takes the image without its trail.

effects.touch: A pressed finger draws the trail. Without touch-action on the image a vertical swipe still scrolls the page, and the trail stops where the scroll takes over; add touch-action: none for drawing without scrolling.

notes.low: At most 32 cells per side.

cost.gpu: One texture read per pixel for the trail plus the picture; three in prism style.
cost.memory: A 64 × 64 half-float texture, 32 KB, besides the image.

effects.name: horizontal
effects.summary: A row of cards on a pinned stage slides sideways as the page scrolls down, its pictures bending with the speed.
effects.looks: While the section is pinned, scrolling down moves the row of cards to the left, one pixel sideways per pixel of scroll. The pictures bow like paper dragged through air, shear or ride a wave across the screen, stretch a little with the speed and settle when the scroll stops; inside each card the picture drifts slower than its frame. The row is a real horizontal scroller, so links, focus, arrow keys and swipes move it too, and the page follows.
effects.target: a row with overflow-x: auto (cards with images inside) on a sticky stage inside its section

params.name: style
params.description: bend bows each picture against the motion; skew shears it, top leading; wave sends one wave across the screen that the cards ride through.

params.name: strength
params.description: How far the pictures bend, shear or wave at full speed; 0 keeps them flat.

params.name: stretch
params.description: Extra width at full speed, as a share of the card; 0 for none.

params.name: parallax
params.description: How far the picture drifts inside its card as it crosses the screen, as a share of the card; 0 for none.

params.name: pace
params.description: Pixels of scroll per pixel the row travels: the effect sets the section height to fit. 0 keeps the height from your CSS.

params.name: reverse
params.description: Starts the row at its end and moves it right.

params.name: ease
params.description: How long the pictures take to follow the speed and flatten again.

params.name: items
params.description: Pictures in the row that get a bending copy.

frames.note: Scroll draws its own frames; ease keeps drawing until the pictures are flat. None at rest.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the row stays a plain horizontal scroller in a section of its own height, and the engine does not load for it.

presence.note: The copies of the pictures fade with the page transition; the row itself is the DOM.

effects.touch: Scrolling the page moves the row, and a sideways swipe on the row scrolls it natively while the page follows.

cost.gpu: One texture read per pixel of each picture, on a plane of 24 rows for bend and wave.
cost.memory: The textures of the pictures in the row.

children.description: Pictures inside the row (items): each gets a copy that bends; text, links and buttons stay DOM.

effects.name: curtain
effects.summary: A cover picture opens from behind a curtain as you scroll: strips slide away, halves part or a liquid edge drains past.
effects.looks: The picture starts covered by a curtain of a solid color or a second picture. As the element scrolls toward the middle of the screen, or as its pinned section scrolls, the curtain opens and casts a soft shadow on the picture at its edge, while the picture settles from a slight zoom. strips slide off one after another, each carrying its slice of the curtain; split parts two halves from the seam, gathering in folds; liquid drains past with a wavy edge and a light rim. Scrolling back closes it again, and with out it closes before the section lets go. Once open it is the picture as it is.
effects.target: img, video; for by pin, on a sticky stage inside a tall section

params.name: style
params.description: strips slide off one after another; split parts two halves from the seam with folds; liquid drains past with a wavy edge.

params.name: by
params.description: view opens it as the element scrolls from the bottom of the screen to its middle; pin follows the pinned section; manual only position.

params.name: direction
params.description: Where the curtain goes: up opens from the bottom. split parts sideways for left and right, up and down for up and down. auto parts split sideways, like a stage curtain, and lifts the others.

params.name: position
params.description: Opening set by hand, 0 shut to 1 open; with view or pin the least opening.

params.name: start
params.description: Progress at which it starts to open.

params.name: end
params.description: Progress at which it is open.

params.name: out
params.description: Progress from which it closes again; 1 keeps it open.

params.name: count
params.description: Strips of strips, folds of each half in split, waves of the liquid edge.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the curtain, or what shows while src loads.

params.name: src
params.description: A second picture to use as the curtain, framed like the image, such as a sketch, a title card or the brand pattern.

params.name: zoom
params.description: Scale the picture settles from; 1 or 0 for none.

params.name: shade
params.description: Depth of the shadow at the edge, the folds of split and the rim of liquid; 0 flat.

params.name: ease
params.description: Smoothing behind scroll; 0 follows it at once (Lenis already smooths it).

params.name: seed
params.description: Shape of the liquid edge.

frames.note: Scroll draws its own frames, ease keeps drawing until it settles. None at rest.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the picture is shown as it is, without the curtain, and the engine does not load for it.

presence.note: Leaving a page closes the curtain, entering opens it up to where the scroll has it. A picture on the first screen waits behind a veil until the curtain is drawn.

effects.touch: The same as with a mouse: it follows the scroll.

cost.gpu: One texture read of the image per pixel, one more with src, and one of a small noise tile for liquid.
cost.memory: The image, the src picture when given and a shared 64 x 64 noise tile.

effects.name: flare
effects.summary: A lens flare or a glossy light sweep over a photo that follows the pointer or the scroll.
effects.looks: A warm light source sits on the photo: a soft glow with a hot core and, in lens style, a row of tinted ghosts along the line from the light through the centre of the frame, like a real lens. In sweep style a glossy band runs through the light at angle and catches the highlights of the picture, the way light slides over chrome or a watch case. The light follows the pointer and fades out when it leaves, travels across the photo with the scroll, or stays put. It is screened over the photo, so it brightens without clipping to white.
effects.target: img, video

params.name: style
params.description: lens draws a glow with ghosts along the axis through the centre; sweep draws a glossy band through the light that brightens the highlights.

params.name: by
params.description: pointer: the light follows the pointer and fades out when it leaves; scroll: it travels across the photo as the page scrolls; fixed: it stays at position.

params.name: strength
params.description: Brightness of the whole flare: 0 turns it off.

params.name: glow
params.description: Radius of the glow as a share of the photo's shorter side: 0 hides the glow.

params.name: ghosts
params.description: Number of ghosts along the axis in lens style, up to 8: 0 shows none.

params.name: streak
params.description: Brightness of a thin anamorphic streak across the frame, in a cool tint: 0 hides it.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the light; the streak takes a cooler shade of it.

params.name: position
params.description: Where the light rests, sits with by fixed and travels through with by scroll, as shares of the box from its top left.

params.name: travel
params.description: With by scroll, how far the light moves across the photo, as a share of its width: 0 keeps it at position.

params.name: angle
params.description: Direction the sweep band runs across, like a CSS gradient angle: 90 is vertical.

params.name: width
params.description: Width of the sweep band as a share of the photo's diagonal.

params.name: rest
params.description: With by pointer, the share of the light kept while the pointer is away, at position: 0 shows the plain photo at rest.

params.name: ease
params.description: Smoothing of the light following the pointer: 0 sticks to it.

params.name: duration
params.description: Length of the fade as the pointer light comes on and goes off.

frames.note: With by pointer, only while the light fades or trails the pointer; with by scroll, only while the page scrolls; none at rest and none with by fixed.

reducedMotion.note: No fade and no smoothing: the pointer light appears, jumps and goes at once. With by scroll the light stays at position.

presence.note: Fades with the page transition; a flight carries the photo without the pointer light.

effects.touch: With by pointer the light follows a finger while it is pressed and goes when it lifts; add touch-action: none to the image to keep a drag from scrolling the page. by scroll works the same on phones.

cost.gpu: One texture read per pixel and a handful of exponentials; the ghosts are math, not reads.
cost.memory: The image only.

effects.name: frost
effects.summary: Frosted glass over a photo, or over the whole page, that the pointer wipes clear and that slowly fogs back.
effects.looks: The photo sits behind frosted glass: blurred, veiled in a pale tint and laced with ice crystals, or, in steam style, a fogged mirror dotted with droplets. Wiping the pointer across it clears a band with a ragged wet edge, which fogs back over refog seconds. Instead of wiping, the glass can clear from the pointer on hover, clear from the middle as the photo comes into view, or clear along with the scroll. On <body> the screen becomes a frozen window: feathers of ice grow in from the edges over a milky veil, glints catch the light near the pointer, and the page under it stays real, readable and clickable. On any other element the same pane covers its box. cover freezes the glass from the edges and thaws it outwards from a point.
effects.target: img, video, body, any element

params.name: style
params.description: frost: ice crystals over a milky layer; steam: a fogged mirror with droplets.

params.name: by
params.description: pointer: the pointer wipes the glass; hover: it clears from where the pointer came in and fogs back when it leaves; view: it clears once as the photo comes into view; scroll: it clears with the scroll between start and end. The pointer wipes in every mode but hover.

params.name: blur
params.description: Blur of the photo behind the glass: 0 keeps it sharp. The pane over a page draws no blur, since it never reads the page.

params.name: strength
params.description: How much the glass veils the photo in color: 0 leaves only the blur.

params.name: grain
params.description: Strength of the ice crystals, or the share of droplets in steam style: 0 is plain glass.

params.name: radius
params.description: Radius of the wipe under the pointer.

params.name: refog
params.description: Seconds a wiped area takes to fog back, and with by hover the fog after the pointer leaves: 0 keeps it clear.

params.name: refill
params.description: How much of the fog comes back over a wiped area: 1 all of it, 0.3 a thin layer that keeps the page readable, 0 none.

params.name: duration
params.description: Length of the clearing with by hover and by view, and of a freeze or thaw.

params.name: start
params.description: With by scroll, the scroll progress at which the clearing begins: 0 as the photo enters at the bottom.

params.name: end
params.description: With by scroll, the scroll progress at which the glass is clear: 0.5 is about the photo centred in the viewport.

params.name: cover
params.description: How much of the glass is frozen: rising, ice grows in from the edges over duration; falling, it thaws outwards from x, y. 0 is bare glass. Live, so a script or a scroll handler can freeze and thaw the page.

params.name: x
params.description: Where a thaw starts, from the left edge of the box (the viewport on <body>).

params.name: y
params.description: Where a thaw starts, from the top edge.

params.name: middle
params.description: How much thinner the ice is in the middle of the pane, so text there stays readable: 0 frosts it evenly, 1 leaves the middle clear. Screens without hover use at least 0.6.

params.name: keep
params.description: A CSS selector of up to six elements the pane keeps a thin veil over, such as the headline and the button, so they stay readable under thick ice. Read when the effect starts; a photo ignores it.

params.name: color
params.description: Tint of the glass, a cold white by default.

params.name: resolution
params.description: Cells across each side of the wipe mask: more gives a finer edge.

frames.note: Only while the pointer wipes, while a wipe fogs back, while a clearing plays and while the ice grows or thaws; none at rest. With by scroll only while the page scrolls.

reducedMotion.note: No animated clearing, freeze or thaw: they jump to where they end. On a photo wiping still works and wiped areas still fog back. The pane over a page is only a faint cold tint without crystals, and nothing wipes it.

presence.note: Fades with the page transition; no wipes are taken while it plays.

effects.touch: On a photo a pressed finger wipes the glass; a scroll takes the gesture, so add touch-action: none to the image to wipe without scrolling. The pane over a page never takes a gesture: every touch clears the ice around it, also while it scrolls, and the middle stays thin. With by hover a tap clears the glass for good. by view and by scroll need no gesture.

notes.low: Blur at most 6 px with 8 reads instead of 16; a 32 × 32 mask. The pane drops its finest crystals.

cost.gpu: On a photo seventeen texture reads per pixel for the blur (nine on low), two of the noise tile and one of the mask; steam adds one for the droplets. The pane reads the noise tile four times and the mask once per pixel of its area, with no blur.
cost.memory: The image, a shared 128 × 128 noise tile and a mask of resolution × resolution bytes × 4.

effects.name: reflection
effects.summary: A soft reflection on a glossy floor under a product photo, without baking it into the image.
effects.looks: Below the image the picture is mirrored, as if the product stood on polished stone or glass: the reflection starts at the product's base, fades out over reach of the image's height and blurs with distance. For a cutout with transparent padding the base is its lowest solid row, so the reflection touches the product, not the edge of the file. A contact shadow can ground it, and a ripple turns the floor into still water.
effects.target: img, video

params.name: strength
params.description: Opacity of the reflection at the base: 0 hides it and leaves only the shadow.

params.name: reach
params.description: How far the reflection runs down, as a share of the element's height.

params.name: blur
params.description: Blur at the far end of the reflection, growing from sharp at the base: 0 is a mirror.

params.name: gap
params.description: Space between the base and the reflection; negative pulls it up.

params.name: trim
params.description: Mirror at the lowest solid row of a transparent picture and at the drawn bottom under object-fit; false mirrors at the bottom of the box.

params.name: ripple
params.description: Sway of a water ripple in the reflection: 0 is a still floor.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Darkness of a soft contact shadow under the base: 0 draws none.

params.name: fps
params.description: Frames a second the ripple draws at while visible.

frames.note: Once when it appears and on layout changes; with a ripple, at most fps a second while visible. None at rest.

reducedMotion.note: The ripple stands still; the reflection itself is not motion.

presence.note: Fades with the page transition.

effects.touch: The same as on desktop: the reflection does not react to input.

notes.low: No blur, one texture read per pixel of the reflection; the ripple at most 15 frames a second.

cost.gpu: Twelve texture reads per pixel of the reflection for the blur and eight for the shadow, only below the image.
cost.memory: The image as a texture; the element itself stays DOM.

effects.name: model
effects.summary: A glTF model fitted into the element, lit, turnable and recolored from markup.
effects.looks: The model from `src` sits centered in the box, lit by a soft studio environment and tone mapped like a product shot, facing the viewer or resting in a three-quarter view seen slightly from above. From that pose it can turn on its own, follow scroll, lean toward the pointer and spin under a drag with a little inertia, staying where the visitor leaves it. A part of it takes the color picked in a group of swatches, blending smoothly to the new one.
effects.target: any element; put a poster inside, it shows without WebGL and until the model is ready

params.name: src
params.description: URL of the GLB or glTF file.

params.name: part
params.description: Material or mesh names to recolor, comma separated; empty keeps the file's colors.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the part, any CSS color.

params.name: swatches
params.description: Selector of a radio group or <select> whose pick recolors the part, as `color` does.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time a color or rest pose change takes.

params.name: scale
params.description: Size in the box: 1 fits the model as it is seen in its rest pose, its near side larger in perspective, centered on what is drawn.

params.name: yaw
params.description: Rest pose turn around the vertical axis; positive turns it as a drag to the right does.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Rest pose tilt toward the viewer; positive shows it from above, -20 to 20.

params.name: spin
params.description: Turns on its own around the vertical; 0 stands still.

params.name: turn
params.description: Turns as the element passes through the viewport.

params.name: tilt
params.description: How far it leans toward the pointer.

params.name: drag
params.description: Turns it under a drag, and with the arrow keys when it has a tabindex.

params.name: clip
params.description: Clip to loop by name, `*` for the first; step keys alone draw only at each key.

params.name: exposure
params.description: Exposure of the tone mapping.

frames.note: Only while something moves: spin, a clip, drag inertia, the tilt settling, or a color or rest pose blending. A clip whose every track steps from key to key, like the hands of a ticking watch, draws one frame per key on a timer while visible, so a watch at rest costs a frame a second. None at rest without spin and clip.

reducedMotion.note: The rest pose shows; spin, clips, scroll turn and tilt stop, and a new rest pose is taken at once. Dragging, arrow keys and color changes still work: the visitor starts them.

presence.note: Leaves by dithering its pixels away while shrinking to 96%, so its opaque materials never switch to transparent mid-transition.

effects.touch: No tilt, nothing hovers. A finger drags the model only when the element has `touch-action: pan-y` or `none`, otherwise the gesture scrolls the page.

cost.gpu: The model as authored, lit by one prefiltered environment. One own material per material of the file.
cost.memory: Geometry and textures of the file, shared with every instance of the same URL, and the environment map.

effects.name: device
effects.summary: A screenshot or a video shown in a 3D phone, tablet, laptop or browser window.
effects.looks: The picture becomes the screen of a device built in 3D with the proportions of the real one: a phone with its camera island and side keys, a tablet, an open laptop with its keyboard and trackpad, or a browser window with its toolbar. params.description: phone with a camera island and side keys, 16:9 to 19.5:9; tablet, 4:3 to 16:10; laptop, open with its keyboard, a 16:10 screen; browser, a window with a toolbar, 5:4 to 12:5.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the body, any CSS color; the browser toolbar takes it too.

params.name: yaw
params.description: Rest turn around the vertical; negative shows the right side.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Rest tilt toward the viewer; positive shows it from above.

params.name: tilt
params.description: How far it leans toward the pointer.

params.name: turn
params.description: Turns it as the element passes through the viewport.

params.name: radius

effects.name: explode
effects.summary: An exploded view of a model: its parts move apart as the section scrolls.
effects.looks: Works on the `model` of the same element. As the visitor scrolls through a sticky section, the parts of the product move apart one after another, the outer ones first, and come back together on the way up, so a page can show what is inside headphones, a watch, a speaker or a chair. The model shrinks a little as it opens so the exploded view stays in its box, and can turn as it opens. Drag, swatches and the rest pose of `model` keep working.
effects.target: an element with the `model` effect: `data-dio="model explode"`, inside a tall `data-dio-section` with a sticky stage

params.name: mode
params.description: radial moves each part away from the center by its own distance; axis stacks the parts in even levels along `axis`, like a watch or a speaker taken apart; extras takes the offsets the modeler wrote as glTF node extras `"explode": [x, y, z]`, in model units.

params.name: by
params.description: What drives it: pin of the sticky section, viewport progress, or `position` alone for a button or a tween.

params.name: pieces
params.description: Node names of the parts to move, comma separated; empty takes the children of the model root (or every node with extras in extras mode).

params.name: axis
params.description: Direction of the axis mode, in model coordinates: x y z.

params.name: spread
params.description: How far the parts move: 1 as the mode lays them out, 0 keeps them in place.

params.name: start
params.description: Progress at which the parts start to move.

params.name: end
params.description: Progress at which they are fully apart.

params.name: position
params.description: How far apart with `by="manual"`: 0 assembled, 1 exploded.

params.name: cascade
params.description: Share of the run by which the parts start one after another, outer ones first.

params.name: twist
params.description: Turns around the vertical while it opens; 0 does not turn.

params.name: ease
params.description: Time the parts take to catch up with the scroll; 0 follows it exactly.

params.name: contain
params.description: Keeps every part inside the box at every step: the model shrinks and recenters as it opens, measured in its rest pose and in perspective.

frames.note: Only on scroll, and while the parts catch up with it for `ease` seconds; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: The exploded view stands still, parts apart and without the turn, wherever the page is scrolled. With `by="manual"` the parts jump to `position` without easing.

presence.note: Nothing of its own: the model leaves by dithering, with its parts where they are.

effects.touch: Scroll drives it, so touch works as on desktop.

cost.gpu: None of its own: the model draws as it does without it.
cost.memory: A few vectors per part.

effects.name: hotspots
effects.summary: Feature callouts pinned to points of a model, real buttons that follow it as it turns.
effects.looks: Goes on a parent of a `model` element. Its children with `data-dio-at` are lifted out of the flow and follow their points on the model while it turns, is dragged or explodes; a label whose point turns to the back of the model fades out and comes back as the point turns round. Focusing a label, by Tab or a click, turns the model to face its point. The labels stay ordinary buttons or links styled by the page, so keyboard, screen readers and the page without WebGL see a plain list.
effects.target: a parent of the `data-dio="model"` element, holding the labels next to it: the drawn model element hides its own children. Labels get a z-index above a canvas over the page; a sticky stage around them needs one too, or the model covers them (a development note names it)

params.name: model
params.description: Selector of the model element, looked up inside the element and then in the page; empty takes the first `data-dio="model"` inside.

params.name: occlude
params.description: normal hides a point label whose point faces away from the viewer (from the center of the model, or along `data-dio-normal`), and a node label once its part is well behind the center, so exploded parts keep theirs; ray hides a label wherever the model covers its point, for rooms, hollow shapes and parts inside a shell, settling a moment after the model stops; none never hides.

params.name: face
params.description: Focusing a label turns the model to face its point.

frames.note: None of its own: labels move in the frames the model draws, written once per frame as a transform and two custom properties. Card sizes are read once and on resize. Focusing a label draws the turn of the model.

reducedMotion.note: Labels follow the model as it stands; focusing a label turns the model at once, without easing.

presence.note: Labels fade with the model during a page transition.

effects.touch: A tap on a label is a click and turns the model to it; a press on a label never starts a drag of the model.

cost.gpu: None: the labels are DOM.
cost.memory: One empty node per label. With `occlude="ray"`, a ray test against the model for two labels per frame and for all of them once it stops.

effects.name: drops
effects.summary: Water drops on glass over a hero or the whole page: rain that beads and runs, or meltwater left by a thaw.
effects.looks: Drops sit on an invisible pane of glass over the page. Small ones rest as beads; heavy ones run down in fits and starts, wander a little, swallow the beads in their way and leave a wet trail with a few beads behind it, which dries over a few seconds. Each drop catches the light in a bright point near its top, glows faintly along its lower edge and darkens at its rim, like a small lens. In rain motion new drops land all the time. In thaw motion the drops appear behind a front that spreads outwards from a point, as if the glass were melting there, and then run down. effects.name: text-reveal
effects.summary: Headings rise, slide up, fade, pop or type into place letter by letter, word by word or line by line.

When the last one lands the element is the real text again: selectable, crisp and styled by your CSS. Text on screen when the page opens is hidden until the effect is ready and then plays the same way; if that takes over 3 seconds it shows as it is. With the scroll trigger such text stays as it is until scrolling reaches it.

effects.name: magnet
effects.summary: Letters become lit 3D slabs that react to the pointer: they push away, turn toward it, rise like a dock or tumble, and spring back.
effects.looks: As the pointer comes near a heading or a link, the letters around it lift off the page as thin glossy slabs. By default they are pushed away and turn their faces from the pointer, the rest of the line making room so no letter runs over its neighbor, and their sides and beveled edges catch the light and each casts its own soft shadow on the page. Other styles turn the letters to face the pointer, raise the ones under it toward the viewer while their neighbors make room, like the macOS dock seen in perspective, or toss them apart, each spinning its own way. Every letter rides a spring, so when the pointer moves on they wobble back into place and the element is the real text again.
effects.target: a heading, a link, a button label or a short line of text. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: repel pushes letters off and turns their faces away from the pointer; attract turns them to face it and draws them in; lift raises the letters under it toward the viewer while neighbors make room; scatter tosses them up and apart, each spinning its own way.

params.name: radius
params.description: Reach of the pointer in em of the text, so a link and a headline feel alike.

params.name: strength
params.description: How far letters move, rise and turn; 0 leaves them in place.

params.name: rotate
params.description: Largest turn of a letter in 3D at the pointer; 0 keeps faces to the viewer.

params.name: stiffness
params.description: Pull of each letter toward where it goes; higher is snappier.

params.name: damping
params.description: Friction of the springs; lower wobbles longer, about 26 does not wobble.

frames.note: Only while letters move toward the pointer or spring back; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the text stays as it is, and the engine does not load for it.

presence.note: Fades with the page.

effects.touch: A finger pressed on the text moves the letters around it until it lifts or the page starts to scroll.

notes.low: The letters are rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: Two instanced draws: five quads per letter for its face and sides, one for its shadow, two texture reads per pixel.
cost.memory: An atlas of the letters at twice their CSS size with room for the shadows, and a relief map of the same size, kept while the element lives.

effects.name: text-glitch
effects.summary: A heading glitches in depth: it breaks into slabs that jump at the viewer, then snaps back flat.
effects.looks: For about two thirds of a second the text breaks into horizontal slabs that jump sideways and towards or away from the viewer, turning in real perspective. Red and cyan layers sit at different depths behind and in front of the letters, so they part as the line tilts. The slice style turns struck slabs into solid blocks with shaded sides; vhs leans the line back with a hologram of scanlines trailing behind it and bends it like worn tape. The pattern jumps twenty times a second; a burst hits twice, with a moment of lost signal between the hits where the text dims, then the element is the real text again, selectable and crisp.
effects.target: a heading, a label, a link or a button with text. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: rgb tilts the line and parts its color layers; slice extrudes blocks; vhs is a hologram.

params.name: trigger
params.description: hover on pointer, focus or tap; interval every few seconds; scroll with speed; load once.

params.name: strength
params.description: How many slabs break and how far they jump and turn; 0 keeps them in place.

params.name: split
params.description: How far the red and cyan layers part in depth and sideways; 0 for none.

params.name: slices
params.description: About how many slabs each line of text breaks into.

params.name: interval
params.description: Average time between bursts with trigger interval, varied by the seed.

params.name: duration
params.description: Length of one burst; from 0.4 s it hits twice with the signal lost between.

params.name: seed
params.description: Which glitch plays: the same seed gives the same one.

frames.note: Only during a burst, and with trigger scroll while the page scrolls fast; none at rest. A timer waits between interval bursts without drawing.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the text is shown as it is, and the engine does not load for it. Sudden flicker can trouble people sensitive to motion and flashing. With motion on, the text dims at most 3 times in any second, under the WCAG flash threshold.

presence.note: Leaving a page the slabs fly at the viewer and drop out one by one; entering they fall back into place.

effects.touch: hover plays a burst on tap and on keyboard focus. The other triggers work the same as with a mouse.

notes.low: The text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: One instanced draw of a quad per layer of a slab, one texture read per pixel; a block adds 14 layers to its slab, the hologram 7.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size with mip levels, kept while the element lives.

effects.name: neon
effects.summary: A heading becomes a 3D neon sign: round glass tubes that stutter on, light the wall and cast a shadow.
effects.looks: The letters become round glass tubes mounted a little in front of the page. Lit, the gas glows white hot along the middle of each tube and saturated at its sides, a highlight runs along the glass, and the tubes throw a soft colored light onto the wall behind them, where their shadow falls too. When the sign comes into view its tubes stutter on one after another like a real sign warming up, and once lit it buzzes now and then. The light that casts the shadow sits above the screen, so the shadow shifts as the page scrolls; a mouse near the sign takes its place, the shadow swings away from it, the highlights slide along the tubes and the sign turns a little toward it. The outline style bends one thin tube along the edge of each letter instead of filling it.
effects.target: a heading, a label or a short line of text, best on a dark background. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: tube makes each stroke a round tube; outline bends a thin tube along the edge.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view turns on as it shows; hover lights on pointer, focus or tap; always stays lit.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the gas and its light, any CSS color; empty uses the text color.

params.name: glow
params.description: Radius of the light thrown on the wall, in ems of the font size; 0 for none.

params.name: strength
params.description: Brightness of the light on the wall and around the tubes; 0 leaves bare tubes.

params.name: depth
params.description: How far the tubes stand off the wall, in ems; 0 mounts them flat on it.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Darkness of the shadow the tubes cast on the wall; 0 for none.

params.name: tilt
params.description: Largest turn of the sign toward a mouse near it, degrees; 0 keeps it still.

params.name: flicker
params.description: How often and how deep the lit sign buzzes and dims; 0 holds it steady.

params.name: broken
params.description: Share of the letters that keep stuttering and going dark; 0 for none.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the flicker, the broken letters and the turn-on; the same seed repeats.

frames.note: Full rate while tubes switch on or off and while the lamp or the sign follows the mouse, 30 a second while a tube flickers, none in between: a timer wakes the sign for its next flicker. With flicker and broken at 0 it draws nothing once lit, except on scroll.

reducedMotion.note: The sign is lit from the start: no turn-on, no flicker, no broken letters, the shadow does not follow the scroll or the mouse, and it draws no frames of its own.

presence.note: Leaving a page the tubes go dark from the last letter back and the glass fades; entering they light up in reading order.

effects.touch: No mouse lamp and no turn: the light stays above the screen. With trigger hover a tap switches the sign on and off.

notes.low: The text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2, and the distance field at half that.

cost.gpu: Three instanced draws of a quad per letter (wall light and shadow, bloom, tubes), at most three texture reads per pixel; nothing is blurred on the GPU.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size, a distance field of it with its direction, and a small atlas of each letter’s light blurred once on the CPU.

effects.name: assemble
effects.summary: Thousands of lit particles fly out of the depth around the page and gather into a heading.
effects.looks: When the heading scrolls into view, a cloud of small glossy beads drifts in front of and behind the page, larger and softer the closer it is to the viewer, then streams along curved paths into the shapes of the letters, left to right, and settles without overshoot. As each letter fills, the real text fades in over its particles, so the heading ends as selectable DOM text with no jump. Tiles that tumble and glint, or streaks of light, can stand in for the beads, and the cloud can rise from below, burst out of a point deep behind the heading or pour in from both sides. With the hover trigger the heading stays made of beads, and the ones under the pointer or a finger lift towards the viewer and spring back.
effects.target: a large heading or a short line of display text. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields. Text with text-shadow, a text stroke, background-clip: text or vertical writing stays as it is

params.name: style
params.description: dots are glossy beads lit from the upper left, for most headings; squares are flat tiles that tumble and glint, like glitter or gold leaf; dashes are streaks of light along the motion, for a fast tech look.

params.name: from
params.description: scatter starts from a cloud around the heading, in front of and behind the page; below rises from under it; center bursts out of a point deep behind its middle; edges pours in from both sides.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view gathers when the heading enters; scroll gathers it towards the middle of the viewport and scatters it again above; hover keeps it as beads the pointer lifts.

params.name: density
params.description: Particles per area of the glyphs; 2 doubles them, up to the tier limit.

params.name: dot
params.description: Size of a particle once it has landed.

params.name: duration
params.description: Flight time of one particle from its start to its place.

params.name: stagger
params.description: Delay between neighboring letters, so they fill in reading order.

params.name: spread
params.description: How far from the text particles start; with the hover trigger, the pointer reach.

params.name: delay
params.description: Wait after the trigger, for a cascade.

params.name: threshold
params.description: Share of the element height in view, above the bottom tenth, before it plays.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the particles in flight; currentColor keeps the color of the text.

params.name: accent
params.description: Second color shimmering through particles in flight; currentColor for none.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the starts, paths and sizes; the same seed gathers the same way.

frames.note: Only while particles fly, while scrolling with the scroll trigger and while lifted beads settle with the hover trigger; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: Off: the text is shown as it is, and the engine does not load for it.

presence.note: Leaving a page, the text breaks back into particles that fly off into the depth; entering, they gather again.

effects.touch: The same as with a mouse; with the hover trigger the beads follow a finger while it presses on the heading.

notes.low: A quarter of the particles, density at most 0.6, and the text rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: One instanced draw of up to 14,000 small quads, and one instanced draw of a quad per letter for the crisp text.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size, and about 80 bytes per particle: about 1.1 MB at the high tier.

effects.name: dust
effects.summary: A heading crumbles into fine sand that lifts off the page and drifts away in depth as it scrolls out, or on a click.
effects.looks: The text breaks into grains made of its own pixels, so the first grain to come loose looks exactly like the ink it leaves. A ragged edge sweeps across the heading from the side the wind blows to; behind it the grains lift off the page towards the viewer, tumble and catch a soft light from the upper left, and stream away along swirling paths, growing and blurring as they come closer and casting faint shadows on the page below. Other motions let the grains rise like ash or blow the heading apart into tiles that fly out of the page in every direction. Scrolling back gathers the sand into the heading again, and at rest the heading is plain DOM text.
effects.target: a large heading, a short line of display text or a dismissible message. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields. Text with text-shadow, a text stroke, background-clip: text or vertical writing stays as it is

params.name: motion
params.description: wind blows the grains along angle in swirling streams, for most headings; rise lets them float up like ash; explode bursts the text into tiles that fly out of the page, front and back.

params.name: trigger
params.description: scroll ties it to the heading leaving the top of the viewport, both ways; click plays it on a click or Enter, then leaves the element empty; view plays it once the heading scrolls out and gathers it back on return.

params.name: density
params.description: Grains per area of the glyphs; 2 doubles them, up to the tier limit.

params.name: dot
params.description: Size of a grain in flight on the page plane; closer grains look larger.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time the click and view triggers take to blow the whole text away.

params.name: angle
params.description: Where the wind blows, counterclockwise from the right; 90 blows straight up.

params.name: turbulence
params.description: Strength of the swirls the grains ride; 0 lets them fly straight.

params.name: depth
params.description: How far the grains travel towards the viewer and back; 0 keeps them flat.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Darkness of the shadows lifted grains cast on the page; 0 turns them off.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the ragged edge, paths and sizes; the same seed blows the same way.

frames.note: While scrolling through the sweep with the scroll trigger, and while the sand flies with the click and view triggers; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: The scroll and view triggers show the text as it is; the click trigger fades the text out in 0.4 s instead.

presence.note: Leaving a page, the heading blows away as sand; entering, the sand gathers back into the text.

effects.touch: The same as with a mouse; a tap plays the click trigger.

notes.low: A quarter of the grains, density at most 0.6, no shadows, and the text rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: Two instanced draws of up to 20,000 small quads, each tracing its path through the flow in five steps, and one instanced draw of a quad per line for the text that is left.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size, a small map of when each grain comes loose, and 48 bytes per grain: about 1 MB at the high tier.

effects.name: extrude
effects.summary: A headline becomes a solid 3D block: beveled letters with lit side walls, seen in perspective, that turn toward the pointer.
effects.looks: The letters keep their font and layout but gain real depth: each one is a block extruded behind its face, with a rounded bevel that catches the light, walls shaded by which way they face and darker toward the back, and a soft shadow on the page behind. The depth recedes in perspective, so letters far from the center show more of their sides. As the pointer moves, the block turns to face it and the light slides over the bevels; with scroll it turns as the heading crosses the viewport. Other styles stack the glyphs as paper layers in your colors, or draw a flat long shadow.
effects.target: a heading or short text in a large, heavy font. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: solid is a lit, beveled block; layers stacks paper cutouts; shadow is a flat long shadow.

params.name: by
params.description: pointer turns it toward the pointer; scroll turns it as the page scrolls; none holds it.

params.name: depth
params.description: How far the depth reaches behind the face at rest; a long shadow runs 5 times this.

params.name: layers
params.description: Number of paper layers behind the face in the layers style.

params.name: tilt
params.description: Largest turn of the block toward the pointer or with the scroll; 0 holds it.

params.name: light
params.description: Where the light comes from as a CSS angle, 0 above and 90 right; depth falls away from it.

params.name: color
params.description: Wall color for solid, paper base for layers, shadow color for shadow; empty derives it.

params.name: colors
params.description: Colors of the paper layers from front to back, repeated; empty uses darker shades.

frames.note: While the depth grows in once, while the pointer moves or the block settles after it, and while scrolling; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: The block is drawn at full depth without growing in, and it does not turn.

presence.note: The block fades with the page.

effects.touch: With by pointer, a touch screen turns the block with the scroll instead, since there is no hover.

notes.low: The text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2, so the depth takes fewer steps.

cost.gpu: One quad over the text and its depth: a march of about one texture read per device pixel of depth, a few reads for the bevel, walls and shadow.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size with mip levels, and a distance field of it at up to a million samples, made once when the page is idle.

effects.name: shimmer
effects.summary: A heading becomes polished chrome, gold, holographic foil or clear glass that catches the light as the pointer moves.
effects.looks: Every letter gets a rounded bevel built from its own shape and is lit as a real material in a small photo studio: a bright sky over a sharp horizon, a dark floor, a softbox overhead and tall strips at the sides. The reflections slide over the letters as the pointer moves and the page scrolls, a light sweeps across them on hover, as they come into view or on a loop, and a soft shadow falls on the page beside them. Chrome and gold are mirror metals, holo is a rainbow foil whose colors shift with the viewing angle and glitter in fine points, and glass is clear in the middle with bright or dark rims and light gathered inside its edges.
effects.target: a large heading, a logo word or a short label in a bold font, on a dark or a light page. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: chrome a mirror metal; gold a warm metal; holo a rainbow foil; glass clear tinted letters.

params.name: trigger
params.description: hover sweeps on pointer, focus or tap; loop every few seconds; view once; pointer a lamp.

params.name: colors
params.description: CSS colors that tint the material, spaces apart; empty uses its own colors.

params.name: bevel
params.description: Width of the rounded edge of each letter in ems of the font size; 0 is flat.

params.name: angle
params.description: Direction the light sweeps in, in degrees like a CSS gradient: 90 is to the right.

params.name: width
params.description: Width of the sweeping light or the pointer lamp; larger is a softer, wider glint.

params.name: speed
params.description: Pace of the sweep and the loop; 0 never sweeps.

params.name: strength
params.description: Brightness of the moving light, the glitter and the light inside glass; 0 for none.

params.name: follow
params.description: How far the reflections turn with the pointer and the scroll; 0 holds them still.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Darkness of the soft shadow the letters cast on the page; 0 for none.

frames.note: None at rest: the material is drawn once and stays. Full rate while the light sweeps and while the reflections settle after the pointer, one frame per scroll or pointer move, and with trigger loop nothing between sweeps.

reducedMotion.note: The material is drawn still: no sweeps, and the reflections no longer follow the pointer or the scroll.

presence.note: The letters and their shadow fade with the page.

effects.touch: The reflections still turn with the scroll; with trigger hover a tap sweeps the light, and with trigger pointer the lamp follows a finger while it touches the text.

notes.low: The text and its bevel are rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: One instanced quad per line of text, three or four texture reads and a few dozen operations per pixel.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size and a half-float map of the bevel, built once on the CPU from a distance field of the letters.

effects.name: rotator
effects.summary: Words take turns in a headline on the faces of a real 3D cube, drum, split flap or folding strip.
effects.looks: The word in the headline sits on a face of a solid shape. Every few seconds the shape turns in perspective to show the next word: a cube rolls up, a drum spins with the words above and below curving away, a split flap falls over its hinge, or a strip folds back into the page while the next one unfolds. Faces darken as they turn away from a lamp above the text and catch a glint as they pass it, and the line around the word eases to the new width. Between turns the word is plain text.
effects.target: an inline element of a heading or paragraph whose children are the words, one element each, such as spans. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: cube rolls a box; drum spins a wheel; flip drops a split flap; fold folds a paper strip.

params.name: trigger
params.description: interval turns on a timer; scroll scrubs the words with the scroll; hover turns on hover.

params.name: axis
params.description: x turns the words up and over; y turns them sideways, along the line.

params.name: interval
params.description: Time each word stays before the next turn, with trigger interval.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time one turn takes.

params.name: depth
params.description: Strength of the perspective; 0 turns the shape flat, without perspective.

params.name: shade
params.description: How much the lamp darkens and lights the turning faces; 0 keeps the text color.

params.name: pause
params.description: Holds the timer while the pointer is over the line or focus is in it.

params.name: loop
params.description: Starts over after the last word; false stops on it.

frames.note: Only while a word turns, and with trigger scroll while scrolling through a turn; none between turns: a timer wakes the next one.

reducedMotion.note: The words still change, but fade into each other in place over a third of a second, without turning.

presence.note: Between turns the word leaves and enters with the page; a turn under way fades with its copy.

effects.touch: The same as with a mouse; with trigger hover a tap turns to the next word, and nothing pauses.

notes.low: The words are rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.

cost.gpu: One instanced draw of two to six textured quads while a word turns; nothing between turns.
cost.memory: A small atlas of the words of the current turn at twice their CSS size, replaced each turn.

effects.name: inflate
effects.summary: Letters puff up into round 3D shapes, like balloons or soft clay, that dent and wobble under the pointer.
effects.looks: Each letter swells into a soft, rounded volume, as if it were filled with air: straight strokes become round tubes, dots become domes and the joints of strokes bulge a little. A studio light from the upper left shades the volume, a glossy highlight runs along it and a soft shadow sits on the page under the letters. As the text comes into view the letters inflate from flat one after another with a springy overshoot. Where the pointer rests the skin dents in and nearby letters lean toward it; a press dents deeper, and on release the letters spring back with a wobble. The soft style looks like matte clay, and the jelly style like translucent gummy candy, clear at the rims and deeper in color where it is thick.
effects.target: a heading, a label or the text inside a button, in a bold or display font. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style
params.description: balloon is glossy foil; soft is matte clay; jelly is clear gummy candy.

params.name: trigger
params.description: view inflates as it shows; hover inflates on pointer, focus or tap; always starts round.

params.name: color
params.description: Color of the letters, any CSS color; empty keeps the color of each letter.

params.name: depth
params.description: How far the letters puff out: 1 makes round tubes, 0 leaves them flat.

params.name: gloss
params.description: Strength of the highlights and of the sheen at the rims; 0 for none.

params.name: squish
params.description: How deep the pointer dents the letters under it; 0 turns the dent off.

params.name: tilt
params.description: Largest lean of the letters near the pointer, degrees; 0 keeps them upright.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time one letter takes to inflate, overshoot included.

params.name: stagger
params.description: Delay between neighboring letters as they inflate.

params.name: delay
params.description: Wait after the trigger, for a cascade.

params.name: threshold
params.description: Share of the element height in view, above the bottom tenth, before it plays.

frames.note: Full rate while letters inflate or deflate and while the dent and the lean follow the pointer and spring back; none at rest, under a still pointer or with the pointer away.

reducedMotion.note: The letters are round from the start and stay still: no inflating, no dent and no lean, and no frames of their own. With trigger hover the label switches between flat and round without motion.

presence.note: Leaving a page the letters go flat and fade; entering, they puff up again.

effects.touch: A finger pressing the letters dents them and they spring back when it lifts; nothing follows a hover. With trigger hover a tap inflates the label and the next one lets it go flat.

notes.low: The text is rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2, and its field holds at most 600,000 texels instead of 1.6 million.

cost.gpu: Two draws: a grid of about one vertex per 3 CSS px for each letter, raised in the vertex shader, with six texture reads per pixel for the light, and one quad for the shadow.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size with mip levels, and a half-float field of it with a margin for the shadow, 8 bytes a texel, built once on the CPU in short steps.

effects.name: ribbon
effects.summary: A headline printed on waving 3D fabric: a flag in the wind, a twisting satin ribbon or slow rippling silk.
effects.looks: The text becomes a sheet of cloth in real 3D, folded by travelling waves and seen in perspective. The folds are lit by their own normals, so the sides turned away from the light darken, crests catch a glossy highlight, and the cloth casts a soft shadow on the page that moves with it. A flag is pinned at its left edge and swings wider toward the free end; a ribbon runs one strip per line, and a twist rolls along it, turning the strip past edge-on to show its tinted back; silk ripples slowly while a sheen sweeps across. The pointer presses a dent into the cloth that follows it.
effects.target: a heading or short text in a large font, optionally with a solid background color and padding. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields

params.name: style

params.description: Surface color behind the text, drawn at rest too; empty uses the element's own background.

effects.name: voxel
effects.summary: A heading built from small lit 3D cubes that tumble in, bounce into place and settle into the text.
effects.looks: When the heading scrolls into view, small cubes in the colors of its letters fall in from above and behind the page, each turning on its own axis, and land in a wave from left to right with a hop and a squash, lower rows first, so the letters stack up like toy blocks. Each cube is lit from the upper left with a beveled edge, and the grooves between neighbors are darker. Once a column has landed the cubes flatten into the face of the text and the real text fades in over them, so the heading ends as selectable DOM text. Toy bricks with studs or flat retro voxels can stand in for the cubes; the voxels stay as they are, and cubes under the pointer pop out toward the viewer, lean out of the bump and spring back.

params.name: depth

params.name: drop
params.description: How far above the text the cubes start; 0 lets them pop up in place.

params.name: duration
params.description: Time one cube takes to fall, land and settle.

params.name: stagger
params.description: Delay of the wave per em of text, left to right; 0 drops every column at once.

params.name: bounce
params.description: Height of the hop and the squash when a cube lands; 0 lands it dead.

params.name: radius
params.description: Reach of the pointer for voxels that stay; 0 turns the pop-out off.

params.name: delay
params.description: Wait after the trigger, for a cascade.

params.name: threshold
params.description: Share of the element height in view, above the bottom tenth, before it plays.

params.name: studs
params.description: Round studs on top of each brick in the bricks style.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the starts and turns of the cubes; the same seed builds the same way.

effects.name: shatter
effects.summary: A heading breaks into lit 3D shards that fly apart and tumble, then fly back together: on a click, on scroll, under the pointer or once in view.
effects.looks: The text box cracks into pieces along seeded fracture lines that follow the letters, and each piece is a real slab with the heading printed on its face. On a click the cracks run out from the point of impact in rings, the pieces nearest it burst out first, and every piece flies off with its own spin, seen through the page camera so the ones coming toward the viewer grow. When the text comes back (hold above 0) the pieces slow down and hang in the air close to the heading, so the break stays in its box; with hold 0 they arc over and fall away under gravity. Turning pieces catch the light: faces brighten and darken, the cut edges glint, the walls show their thickness, and lifted pieces cast soft shadows on the page. Glass breaks into thin clear panes with green edges and reflections, stone into thick chunks with rough walls and a puff of dust, paper into torn scraps with pale fibers that flutter down and show their blank backs. After a pause the pieces fly back along their own paths and lock into place.
effects.target: a large heading or short line of display text. Not img, video, canvas, svg or form fields. Text with text-shadow, a text stroke, background-clip: text or vertical writing stays as it is

params.name: style
params.description: glass is thin clear panes; stone is thick rough chunks with dust; paper is torn scraps.

params.name: trigger
params.description: click breaks where clicked; scroll as it leaves; hover lifts pieces; view flies it in.

params.name: pieces
params.description: About how many pieces the text box is cut into; pieces with no ink are left out.

params.name: strength
params.description: Speed the pieces leave with, and how high they lift with the hover trigger.

params.name: spin
params.description: How fast the pieces tumble; 0 keeps them flat to the page as they fly.

params.name: gravity
params.description: Pull that bends the paths down; 0 lets the pieces drift off in a straight line.

params.name: depth
params.description: Thickness of a piece, times the thickness of its style; 0 makes flat pieces.

params.name: hold
params.description: Time the click trigger waits before the pieces fly back; 0 leaves the text gone.

params.name: seed
params.description: Picks the fracture lines, paths and spins; the same seed breaks the same way.

frames.note: While the pieces fly, fly back or settle, and while scrolling through the break with the scroll trigger; none at rest.

reducedMotion.note: The click trigger fades the text out instead, and back in after hold; the other triggers keep the text as it is.

presence.note: The pieces fade with the page.

effects.touch: A tap breaks it with the click trigger; with the hover trigger a finger on the text lifts the pieces under it.

notes.low: At most 24 pieces, a shorter march through stone, no dust, and the text rastered at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel instead of 2.
notes.medium: At most 64 pieces and a shorter march through stone.

cost.gpu: One draw of every piece as a prism of a few dozen triangles, back to front, with a short march through stone; one draw of their shadows and one of up to 420 dust motes.
cost.memory: A canvas of the text at twice its CSS size and two small float textures of the pieces: a few MB for a large heading.

effects.name: tunnel
effects.summary: The phrases of a pinned section stand one behind another in real depth, and the scroll flies the camera through them.
effects.looks: The first phrase sits where the page has it, and the next ones wait further back in the dark, smaller and fainter. Scrolling moves the camera forward: the phrase in front grows in perspective, blurs and passes the viewer, and the next one comes out of the distance and slows down to be read. In a tunnel the phrases wait on the floor and ceiling of a corridor drawn with faint lines and swing to face the reader as they arrive, and while one holds in focus nothing behind it crosses it; zoom flies straight through them; in a spiral they wait along a turning helix. A fast scroll streaks the letters toward the edges. At the end of the section the last phrase stays as plain text.

effects.name: emboss
effects.summary: Letters pressed into or raised out of paper, leather, brushed metal, stone or plaster, lit by a light that follows the pointer.
effects.looks: The element becomes a piece of material in its own background color, with the text as a real relief built from the shape of every letter: raised like a book cover, pressed in like a business card, printed into thick paper with ink in the bottom, or stood up on a wax seal. A lamp follows the pointer and drifts as the page scrolls, so the walls of the letters catch the light on one side and fall into shadow on the other, the letters cast soft shadows on the surface, and the fibres, grain, brushing or speckle of the material glint across the whole card. Small print stays printed in its color.
